chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning tayammum.
He said: “You strike the earth with your two palms, then shake them off, and wipe your face and your two hands.”

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Likewise, the menstruating woman, the woman in post-partum bleeding, and the woman with istiḥāḍah do this in place of ghusl when they do not find water or when its use would harm them.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: ritual dry ablution performed as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the earth, the surface struck for performing tayammum
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath, for which tayammum may serve as a substitute in certain circumstances
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: the woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular bleeding
key_terms.بِكَفَّيْكَ: with your two palms, indicating the instrument used in tayammum
key_terms.وَجْهَكَ: your face, one of the parts wiped in tayammum
key_terms.يَدَيْكَ: your two hands, the other parts wiped in tayammum

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed, and when may it replace ghusl for women?
ai.summary: This report explains the manner of tayammum: one strikes the earth with both palms, shakes them off, then wipes the face and hands. It also states that women requiring ghusl due to menstruation, post-partum bleeding, or istiḥāḍah may perform tayammum instead when water is unavailable or harmful to use.
